summary: Amun-Re is a two-phase Knizia auction game where players bid for Egyptian provinces then decide how much to invest in farming income versus building pyramids for prestige. The tight economic tension and blind sacrifice mechanic make every round a careful balancing act.
criticised: can feel dry and abstract thematically
auctions can be swingy if players misjudge province values
two-phase structure can feel repetitive over many rounds

interaction.kind: auction and bidding for shared provinces
interaction.detail: Players bid directly against each other for the same limited set of provinces each round, competing head-to-head for resources, then develop pyramids and farms on their own individual boards.

sources: pyramid stones scored at end of epoch 1
pyramid stones scored at end of epoch 2 (final)
scoring.how_you_win: You bid for provinces, farm and trade for gold, and spend that gold on pyramid stones and secret power cards; pyramids are scored at the end of each of the two epochs and power-card sets add bonus points, with the highest total after epoch two winning.
